description: Each person adds one idea in turn so that nobody dominates and quiet voices are heard.
Build on the last idea by starting with "yes and" before adding to it.
Propose ideas as if you were a competitor or a customer or a regulator.
Everyone writes ideas silently for a few minutes before any discussion.
Substitute then combine then adapt then modify then put to another use then eliminate then reverse.
Generate questions (who and what and when and where and why and how) instead of answers.
List the parameters of the problem and the options for each and combine across columns.
Look at the problem in turn from facts and feelings and risks and benefits and creativity and process.
Put the topic in the centre and branch out themes and sub-themes to see gaps.
Ask how to cause the problem or make it worse and then flip each answer into a solution.
Rephrase the problem as "How might we..." to open it up without implying a solution.
Ask why repeatedly to move from a symptom to a root cause that can be addressed.
Describe the progress a person is trying to make and the situation they hire a solution in.
Treat the biggest constraint as a feature and ask what it would enable.
Ask how a very different industry solves the same underlying problem.
Look for how living systems handle the same need and borrow the pattern.
Describe the product as a metaphor (a library or a kitchen or an airport) and mine it for features.
Imagine ten times the users or one tenth of the budget and see what breaks or appears.
Ask what the experience would be if the user had to do nothing at all.
Collect deliberately terrible ideas then look for the useful kernel in each one.
Write the headline you want in two years and work backwards to what had to happen.
Assume it failed and list the reasons so that they can be prevented now.
Each person places a few dots on the ideas they value most to show the group's weight.
Place ideas on a grid of value against effort and start with high value and low effort.
Sort the ideas into what to do now and what next and what later to give them a sequence.
